critique.good: The paired name columns have equal weight, prices stay on one line, and all headers are intact. The description has enough room to form readable phrases.
critique.problems: The final dish names wrap heavily, especially the Thai name, while the first and last descriptions make their rows tall. The two name columns feel cramped beside the price column.
critique.cause: At 80px each, the name columns have 59px of text space. The 121px description column has 100px, which still requires several lines for the longer descriptions; the 78px price column is as wide as either name column.

critique.good: The wider paired name columns make the dish names easier to scan, and prices remain intact and aligned.
critique.problems: The description becomes a narrow vertical stack of short fragments, its header wraps, and the resulting tall rows leave extensive empty space in the other columns. This makes it harder to read across each row.
critique.cause: The 100px name columns consume space needed by the description, which is only 81px wide with 60px of text space.

critique.good: The wider description produces more coherent phrases and a shorter, more balanced table than r0B. Prices and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: Both name columns are cramped: even the first dish names wrap, and the last Lao name becomes a tall stack. That weakens the pairing of the two names and makes dish identification slower.
critique.cause: The 70px name columns provide only 49px of text space, while the 141px description column takes a larger share of the available width.

critique.good: The Thai and Lao names have equal visual weight, prices stay on one line, and each row reads across clearly. The description uses the height created by wrapped dish names.
critique.problems: The first and last descriptions make their rows tall, while the last Thai dish name breaks into three lines.
critique.cause: The 125px description column leaves 104px for text; the 78px Thai name column leaves 57px.

critique.good: The paired name columns remain balanced, and prices stay intact and easy to compare.
critique.problems: The wider name columns do not noticeably improve the longest Thai name, while the first description becomes five lines and creates a particularly tall row.
critique.cause: Increasing each name column to 85px reduces the description column to 111px, leaving only 90px for its text.

critique.good: The wider description column improves the first row, and the paired name columns remain balanced.
critique.problems: Every price wraps its currency unit onto a second line, weakening price comparison and making the narrow price column feel crowded. The last description still takes four lines.
critique.cause: The 69px price column leaves only 48px for text, less than the 57px needed for the longest price. The 130px description column still leaves only 109px for text.

critique.good: The two dish-name columns have equal weight, prices stay on one line, and the description has enough room for the first row to remain relatively compact. The row boundaries make each bilingual pairing easy to follow.
critique.problems: The last dish name is fragmented into three lines in both languages, while its description takes four lines. The tall final row creates a dense block of short lines.
critique.cause: The 76px name columns leave 55px for text; the 129px description column leaves 108px.

critique.good: The paired name columns remain balanced, prices stay intact, and the wider description produces a more comfortable first-row line pattern. The overall row heights match r2A.
critique.problems: The narrow name columns still break the final dish names into three short lines, and the last description remains four lines tall. The small gain in description width does not reduce the table height.
critique.cause: Reducing each name column to 73px leaves 52px for text; increasing the description to 135px leaves 114px, still insufficient to remove a line from the tallest description.

critique.good: The Thai name column has a little more breathing room, the Lao column retains the width used in r2A, and prices remain intact.
critique.problems: The first description gains a line, making its row taller without visibly improving the dish names. The narrower description also creates more short lines and a less even distribution of space across the row.
critique.cause: The 80px Thai name column takes space from the description, which falls to 125px and leaves only 104px for text.

understanding.purpose: A bilingual Thai–Lao menu pairs dish names with prices and Thai descriptions.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the paired names to identify a dish, then read across the row for its price and description; aligned prices also support comparison.
groups: Columns 1 and 2 give corresponding dish names in Thai and Lao and should have comparable visual weight.
Columns 3 and 4 provide the price and description for each paired dish.
keep_intact: Individual Thai and Lao words and dish-name components
Each price and its currency unit
may_wrap: Multiword dish names in both languages
Thai descriptions, using the height created by wrapped names where possible

bad.why: All three prices break between the amount and บาท, making a short, frequently compared value unnecessarily difficult to scan.

final.rationale: r3B keeps the prices on one line and gives the long descriptions enough space to avoid the particularly tall first row seen in r1B and r2C. The two language columns remain close in width, reflecting their equivalent roles, while the description receives the largest share. The third dish still wraps in both languages, but the row remains readable as a unit.

general: Keep short values that readers compare, such as prices and their units, together where possible.
Give related columns comparable visual weight while reserving more space for substantially longer prose.
Judge wrapping across the whole row: saving space in one column can make the entire row taller.
specific: The price column needs approximately 78px here to keep the displayed amounts and บาท together.
A description width around 129–132px produces the same row heights in the tested designs while leaving the first dish names intact.

final.tradeoffs: r2A gives the two language columns equal widths; r3B gives a few more pixels to the description. A designer might prefer the symmetry of r2A, since both render at the same height.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative estimates from the supplied renderings, not verified continuous intervals. The exact wrapping thresholds between tested widths could differ.

A.why: The description has useful space, but every price splits across two lines and the longest Thai dish name wraps to three.

B.why: Prices stay together and the two dish-name columns have similar widths. The narrower description column creates several short lines, especially in the first row.

C.why: Prices stay on one line and the description has enough room for a reasonably steady reading rhythm. The longest Thai and Lao names each wrap to three lines.

D.why: Prices and dish names have room, but the description is squeezed into a narrow column with many short fragments, making the rows tall and harder to scan.

E.why: Prices remain intact, and the description has a workable width without giving up the balance between the Thai and Lao name columns. Both longest names still wrap to three lines.

F.why: The wider description reads more comfortably, but all three prices break between the number and currency, weakening a useful column for comparison.

reviews.unsure: C and E are very close at this image size; their small width differences do not produce a clear reading advantage.

A.why: The very narrow description column produces long stacks of short lines and excessive row height, while the price column has room to spare.

B.why: The descriptions have useful space, but every price wraps its currency onto a second line, weakening quick price comparisons.

C.why: Prices stay together and the two menu-name columns are balanced, though the narrower description column makes the first row relatively tall.

D.why: Prices stay on one line and the wider description column gives the rows a comfortable rhythm; the longer menu names still wrap considerably.

E.why: The description column reads well, but the narrow price column splits every amount from its currency.

F.why: Prices stay intact and descriptions have room to breathe, though the longer Thai and Lao names wrap across several lines.

reviews.unsure: D and F are very close in appearance; the small difference in their column widths does not produce a clear overall winner.
